sentences.text: Budget 2019 is a strategic plan to allocate resources to build a strong, united Singapore.

sentences.text: Digital Defence has now been incorporated as the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sections.label: Singapore economy and median income
sections.summary: The Singapore economy grew by 3.2% in 2018, and real median income grew by 3.6% per year over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In tandem with the global expansion, the Singapore economy grew by 3.2% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the real median income of Singaporeans has grown by 3.6% per year.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps launched
sections.summary: In Budget 2016, the Industry Transformation Maps were launched to drive transformation at company, industry and economy-wide levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In Budget 2016, we launched the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), which drive transformation at the company, industry, and economy-wide levels.

sections.label: All 23 ITMs launched
sections.summary: All 23 ITMs have been launched, covering about 80% of the economy, with productivity growing 3.6% per year in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: After three years of intensive work, I am glad that all 23 ITMs have been launched, covering about 80% of our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Productivity, as measured by real value-added per actual hour worked, grew by 3.6% per year in the past last three years, higher than the 1.6% per annum growth recorded in the preceding three years, from 2012 to 2015.

sections.label: Startup support and venture capital deals
sections.summary: Support ranges from co-investments and proof-of-concept grants to mentorship and physical space, with over 220 venture capital deals per year worth close to US$4.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Such support ranges from co-investments and proof-of-concept grants to mentorship and physical space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: There are now over 220 venture capital deals per year in Singapore, worth close to US$4.2 billion.

sections.label: SME Co-Investment Fund III
sections.summary: An additional $100 million will establish the SME Co-Investment Fund III, expected to bring in at least $200 million of additional funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So far, the Government’s investments have catalysed approximately $1.3 billion of additional funding for our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, I will set aside an additional $100 million to establish the SME Co-Investment Fund III.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As part of the CIP, it will catalyse investment in Singapore-based SMEs that are ready to scale up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect that this will bring in at least $200 million of additional funding.

sections.label: Single Enterprise Financing Scheme
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore's existing financing schemes will be streamlined into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme covering trade, working capital, fixed assets, venture debt, mergers and acquisitions, and project financing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To make it simpler for companies, we will streamline the existing financing schemes offered by Enterprise Singapore into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme that will cover trade, working capital, fixed assets, venture debt, mergers and acquisitions, and project financing.

sections.label: SME Working Capital Loan extension
sections.summary: The Government will take on up to 70% of risk for bank loans to young companies and extend the SME Working Capital Loan scheme till March 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will take on up to 70% of the risk for bank loans to these young companies, compared to the current 50% under most existing loan schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support viable SMEs in their day-to-day operations, I will extend the SME Working Capital Loan scheme, for about two more years, till March 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since its launch in June 2016, the scheme has catalysed more than $2.5 billion of loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect the extension to catalyse a further $1.8 billion.

sections.label: Industry digital plans for sectors
sections.summary: Accountancy, sea transport and construction will get their own industry digital plans, with more sectors added later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, accountancy, sea transport and construction will get their own industry digital plans, with more sectors to be added later.

sections.label: Business sans Borders platform pilot
sections.summary: MAS and IMDA will jointly pilot a cross-border innovation platform for SMEs called Business sans Borders, with an Artificial Intelligence-enabled marketplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: MAS and the Info-communications Media Development Authority (IMDA) will also jointly pilot a cross-border innovation platform for SMEs, known as the Business sans Borders, with an Artificial Intelligence-enabled marketplace to help our SMEs match with buyers and vendors globally.

sections.label: Training and Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: Investments in career support reached more than $1.1 billion in FY2017, training participation grew from 35% to 48%, and over 76,000 jobseekers found employment from 2016 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our investments in supporting our people in their careers, including Adapt and Grow initiatives and continuing education and training, reached more than $1.1 billion in FY2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The percentage of residents in the labour force who participated in training grew from 35% in 2015, to 48% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2018, more than 76,000 jobseekers found employment through the Adapt and Grow initiative.

sections.label: New PCPs in growth areas
sections.summary: Over 100 PCPs have been launched since 2007, and new PCPs in blockchain, embedded software and prefabrication will be launched this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since the establishment of the PCP in 2007, over 100 PCPs have been launched in about 30 sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will launch new PCPs relating to blockchain, embedded software, and prefabrication to prepare our people to move into new growth areas.

sections.label: Enterprise Development Grant worker outcomes
sections.summary: From 1 April 2020, all Enterprise Development Grant-supported transformation efforts must include positive worker outcomes such as wage increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Starting from 1 April 2020, all transformation efforts supported by Enterprise Singapore's Enterprise Development Grant must include positive outcomes for workers, such as wage increases.

sections.label: Number risen 3% per annum
sections.summary: The number has risen by about 3% per annum, or 34,000, in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The number has risen by about 3% per annum or 34,000 in the last three years.

sections.label: Services sector quota reductions
sections.summary: The services sector DRC will be cut from 40% to 38% in 2020 and 35% in 2021, and the S Pass Sub-DRC from 15% to 13% and 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: After much deliberation, we will adjust the workforce quota for the services sector and reduce the services sector Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) in two steps, from 40% to 38% on 1 January 2020, and to 35% on 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also reduce the services sector S Pass Sub-DRC in two steps, from 15% to 13% on 1 January 2020, and to 10% on 1 January 2021.

sections.label: Grant funding support extended
sections.summary: Enhanced 70% funding for the Enterprise Development Grant is extended to 31 March 2023, and the Productivity Solutions Grant gets the same and expanded training cost scope.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, the 70% funding support level for the Enterprise Development Grant was due to lapse after 31 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will now extend this enhanced funding support for three more years, up to 31 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, we will do the same for the Productivity Solutions Grant, and expand its scope to support up to 70% of the out-of-pocket cost for training.

sections.label: Marine shipyard levy increase deferred
sections.summary: The earlier-announced increase in Foreign Worker Levy rates for the Marine Shipyard and Process sectors is deferred for another year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As the Marine Shipyard and Process sectors have only begun showing early signs of recovery, I will defer the earlier-announced increase in Foreign Worker Levy rates for these sectors for another year.

sections.label: EU-Singapore trade agreements consent
sections.summary: The EUSFTA and EUSIPA received the European Parliament's consent with a clear majority last week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Just last week, the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EUSFTA) and the EU Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (EUSIPA) received the European Parliament’s consent with a clear majority.

sections.label: Networked Trade Platform launch
sections.summary: Last year, the Networked Trade Platform was launched to streamline trade processes and provide a one-stop information management system for traders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, I launched the Networked Trade Platform (NTP) to streamline trade processes and provide a one-stop information management system for traders.

sections.label: R&D investment under RIE2020
sections.summary: R&D investment continues, with $19 billion set aside under the five-year Research, Innovation, and Enterprise 2020 plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, we will continue to invest in R&D to support the push to make innovation pervasive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have set aside $19 billion as part of our five-year Research, Innovation, and Enterprise 2020 (RIE2020) plan.

sections.label: Site productivity improvement
sections.summary: Site productivity has improved by about 15% over the last eight years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Site productivity has improved by about 15% over the last eight years.

sections.label: Agri-food start-up co-investment partners
sections.summary: SEEDS Capital appointed seven partners to co-invest in Singapore-based agri-food start-ups, to catalyse more than $90 million of investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To tap on the demand for high-quality food and to build on our progress, Enterprise Singapore's investment arm, SEEDS Capital, has appointed seven partners to co-invest in Singapore-based agri-food start-ups, to catalyse more than $90 million of investments.

sections.label: Corporate labs with major companies
sections.summary: Last year, four corporate labs were opened with Applied Materials, HP, Wilmar, and Surbana-Jurong to work on advanced manufacturing, biochemicals and smart cities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, we opened four corporate labs with major companies – Applied Materials, HP, Wilmar, and Surbana-Jurong – to work on advanced manufacturing, biochemicals and smart cities.

sections.label: Centres of Innovation investment
sections.summary: Singapore will keep investing in Centres of Innovation at IHLs and research institutes, including new aquaculture and energy centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To keep the momentum going, we will continue to invest in Centres of Innovation at our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and research institutes, and to support companies in innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore is collaborating with industry partners to establish a Centre of Innovation in Aquaculture at Temasek Polytechnic to promote aquaculture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will also launch a Centre of Innovation in Energy at NTU, building on earlier investments at the Energy Research Institute at NTU (ERI@N).

sections.label: Global Ready Talent Programme
sections.summary: Local and overseas internships will merge into a Global Ready Talent Programme, which also supports postings abroad for experienced Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For students who are currently in IHLs, we will combine the current local and overseas internship programmes into a single Global Ready Talent Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The programme will also support high-growth Singapore firms to send Singaporeans, with up to three years of working experience, for postings in key markets such as Southeast Asia, China, and India.

sections.label: Investors in ASEAN enterprises
sections.summary: Investors on the MATCH platform expressed interest to invest up to US$12 billion in ASEAN fintech, ICT and medtech enterprises over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As part of this Festival, the Global Investor Summit brought together investors on our Meet ASEAN's Talents and Champions (MATCH) platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These investors expressed an interest to invest up to US$12 billion in ASEAN enterprises in fintech, info-communications technology, and medtech over the next three years.

sections.label: Budget 2019 economic capability measures
sections.summary: Singapore expects to spend $4.6 billion over three years on economic capability-building measures, supporting workers and firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will position Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect to spend $4.6 billion over the next three years on the new and enhanced economic capability-building measures in Budget 2019, and to support Singaporean workers: $3.6 billion will go towards helping our workers to thrive amid industry and technological changes; and $1 billion will go towards helping firms build deep enterprise capabilities.

sections.label: Social Ministries expenditure doubled
sections.summary: Social Ministries' expenditures doubled from $15 billion in FY2009 to $30 billion in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Social Ministries’ expenditures have doubled from $15 billion in FY2009, to $30 billion in FY2018.

sections.label: Preschool and education subsidies
sections.summary: Government spent about $1 billion on preschool in 2018 and subsidises over 90% of educating children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government spent about $1 billion on the preschool sector in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is more than two and a half times of the $360 million that we spent back in 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government subsidises over 90% of the total cost of educating our children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This means that a child entering primary school in 2018 will receive over $130,000 in education subsidies by the time he or she completes secondary education.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot family support
sections.summary: Since the pilot began in 2016, KidSTART has supported more than 900 families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since the pilot began in 2016, more than 900 families have been supported by KidSTART.

sections.label: UPLIFT scholarship for Independent Schools
sections.summary: The UPLIFT scholarship gives eligible lower income students in Independent Schools $800 per year for out-of-pocket expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A recent initiative is the UPLIFT scholarship for Independent Schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will provide a monetary award of $800 per year for eligible lower income students in Independent Schools, to cover their out-of-pocket expenses.

sections.label: Enhanced WIS income cap and payouts
sections.summary: From January 2020 the WIS income cap rises to $2,300 and payouts increase, costing close to $1 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: From January 2020, the qualifying income cap will be raised from the current $2,000 to $2,300 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The maximum annual payouts will also be increased by up to $400.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, workers aged 60 and earning $1,200 a month will now receive $4,000 per year from WIS, or almost 30% of their wages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These enhancements will cost an additional $206 million a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, we expect the enhanced WIS to cost close to $1 billion a year, and benefit almost 440,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: CHAS subsidy enhancements at GP clinics
sections.summary: CHAS subsidies at GP clinics will be enhanced by extending CHAS to all Singaporeans for chronic conditions and other changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over 97% of existing CHAS and Pioneer Generation cardholders have access to more than one CHAS clinic within 10 minutes from their homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will enhance CHAS subsidies at GP clinics in three ways: first, as the Prime Minister announced at the National Day Rally last year, we will extend CHAS to cover all Singaporeans for chronic conditions, regardless of income; second, lower- to middle-income Singaporeans who are CHAS Orange cardholders currently receive CHAS subsidies for chronic conditions only.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will extend subsidies for common illnesses to this group; and third, we will increase the subsidies for complex chronic conditions.

sections.label: Expected CHAS subsidy payouts
sections.summary: With these changes, more than $200 million a year is expected to be paid out in CHAS subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With these changes, we expect to pay out more than $200 million a year in CHAS subsidies.

sections.label: CareShield Life lifetime coverage
sections.summary: CareShield Life will provide lifetime coverage with monthly payouts of at least $600 for severe disability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: CareShield Life will provide lifetime coverage, with higher monthly payouts of at least $600 a month for those who become severely disabled.

sections.label: Long-Term Care Support Fund
sections.summary: The Government will put $5.1 billion, from $2 billion earmarked last year and $3.1 billion set aside this year, into a new Long-Term Care Support Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, I earmarked $2 billion for premium subsidies and other forms of support for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, I will set aside another $3.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will put this $5.1 billion into a new Long-Term Care Support Fund.

sections.label: PAssion Silver card top-up
sections.summary: All Merdeka Generation seniors will receive a one-time $100 top-up to their PAssion Silver cards to support active lifestyles.

sentences.text: First, to support their active lifestyles, all Merdeka Generation (MG) seniors will receive a one-time $100 top-up to their PAssion Silver cards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, we will provide a MediSave top-up of $200 per year for five years.

sections.label: Outpatient care subsidies

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Third, MG seniors will receive additional subsidies for outpatient care, for life.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium subsidies

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Fourth, MG seniors will have additional MediShield Life premium subsidies for life.

sections.label: CareShield Life participation incentives

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)

sections.label: Merdeka Generation package cost estimate
sections.summary: MOF and MOH sized the budget taking this into account, estimating the package will cost over $8 billion in current dollars over the Merdeka Generation's lifetimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) and MOH, in sizing the budget for these benefits, have taken this into account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We estimate that the package will cost over $8 billion, in current dollars, over the Merdeka Generation's lifetimes.

sections.label: Sustaining youth and public officer volunteerism

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We want to sustain this momentum as they move to IHLs, and later into the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are working with Youth Corps Singapore to nurture youth community leaders in our IHLs, who can in turn rally their peers to be involved in the community on a sustained basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To enable more of them to do so, we will work with community partners and companies to encourage volunteerism among older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Third, the Government is encouraging all public officers to volunteer, under the Public Service Cares initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: More than 85% of public officers are making monthly donations.

sentences.text: The new Bicentennial Community Fund will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for donations made to IPCs in FY2019.

sections.label: Bicentennial Bonus introduction

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, I will introduce a $1.1 billion Bicentennial Bonus.

sections.summary: The Bicentennial Bonus includes a GST Voucher – Cash (Bicentennial Payment) of up to $300, a Workfare Bicentennial Bonus, and a 50% Personal Income Tax Rebate capped at $200 for YA2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Bicentennial Bonus has several components  : For lower-income Singaporeans, I will provide additional help with their daily living expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)

sentences.text: In addition, lower-income workers who received WIS payments will get a Workfare Bicentennial Bonus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will provide a 50% Personal Income Tax Rebate, subject to a cap of $200, for YA2019.

sections.label: Edusave top-up for students

sentences.text: This helps to pay for school enrichment activities, to better develop students holistically.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will provide a $150 top-up to their Edusave accounts.

sentences.text: We will also provide additional support for older Singaporeans, who are near retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will provide a CPF top-up of up to $1,000 for eligible Singaporeans aged 50 to 64 years old in 2019, who have less than $60,000 of retirement savings in their CPF accounts.

sections.label: Climate Action Plan measures
sections.summary: The 2016 Climate Action Plan sets out strategy for mitigating and adapting to climate change impacts, with Terminal 5 and Pulau Tekong measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our Climate Action Plan, which was launched in 2016, sets out the strategy for mitigating and adapting to the impacts of climate change, especially on our infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Changi Airport Terminal 5 will also be built at 5.5 metres above mean sea level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The use of polders and dikes is already being piloted on Pulau Tekong.

sections.label: Diesel excise duty and taxi tax
sections.summary: Diesel excise duty rises 10 cents per litre to 20 cents, while annual Special Tax on diesel taxis is permanently cut by $850.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To continue the restructuring of diesel taxes, I will raise excise duty for diesel by 10 cents per litre, to 20 cents per litre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At the same time, I will permanently reduce the annual Special Tax on diesel taxis by $850.

sections.label: Road tax rebates for diesel vehicles
sections.summary: Commercial diesel vehicles get a 100% road tax rebate for one year and partial rebate for another two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help businesses adjust, I will provide a 100% road tax rebate for one year and partial road tax rebate for another two years, for commercial diesel vehicles.

sections.label: Differentiated fiscal strategy
sections.summary: New investments will use a differentiated fiscal strategy, with one approach for major infrastructure and another for recurrent social and security expenditures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While our nation's needs are growing significantly, we must continue to take a disciplined and prudent approach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will pursue new investments using a differentiated fiscal strategy, taking one approach for major infrastructure investments, and another for recurrent social and security expenditures.

sections.label: Borrowing for large lumpy expenditures
sections.summary: Borrowing is fairer and more efficient for large lumpy expenditures whose benefits span many generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For these large and lumpy expenditures where the benefits span many generations of Singaporeans, paying for them through some borrowing is fairer and more efficient.

sections.label: Guarantee for Changi East borrowings
sections.summary: The Government, with the President's concurrence, will guarantee Changi East borrowings to lower financing costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To lower financing costs, the Government, with the President's concurrence, will provide a guarantee for Changi East borrowings.

sections.label: GST relief and alcohol concessions tightened
sections.summary: GST relief for goods bought overseas is reduced to $100 and $500, and alcohol duty-free concession is cut to two litres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For travellers who spend less than 48 hours outside Singapore, the value of goods bought overseas that can enjoy GST relief will be reduced from $150 to $100.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For travellers who spend 48 hours or more outside Singapore, the relief quantum will be reduced from $600 to $500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also tighten the alcohol duty-free concession for travellers from three litres to two litres.

sections.label: FY2018 and FY2019 budget position
sections.summary: FY2018 expects a $2.1 billion surplus and FY2019 a $7.1 billion basic deficit, with funds set aside for long-term needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For FY2018, we expect an overall budget surplus of $2.1 billion, or 0.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is a $2.7 billion increase from the $0.6 billion deficit forecasted a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This was due to the unexpected two-year suspension of the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High-Speed Rail Project and higher-than-expected Stamp Duty collections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: When we exclude the Government’s top-ups to funds and Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) from past Reserves, we expect a basic deficit of $7.0 billion, or 1.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For FY2019, our Budget position remains expansionary, with a basic deficit of $7.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Ministries’ total expenditures are expected to be $80.3 billion, 1.6% higher than in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are setting aside funds to meet Singaporeans' long-term needs, including $6.1 billion for the Merdeka Generation Package and $5.1 billion for long-term care support.

sections.label: Approval of Government financial policy
sections.summary: The Question seeks Parliament's approval of the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2019 to 31 March 2020, and debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2019 to 31 March 2020." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
